questions.exp: Particles of the fragrance move and mix with the moving air particles, spreading out by diffusion.

questions.q: Riya dissolves 20 g of salt in 180 g of water. What is the concentration of the solution by mass percentage?
Arjun makes an electromagnet by winding insulated wire around an iron nail and connecting it to a cell. It picks up only 3 pins. Which change will help it pick up more pins?
questions.a: Replacing the iron nail with a plastic pen
questions.b: Using a weaker cell to reduce current
questions.c: Increasing the number of turns of wire
questions.d: Removing the iron nail from the coil
questions.exp: More turns of wire (or more current, with an iron core) make the magnetic field of an electromagnet stronger.

questions.q: Who founded the Maratha kingdom and was crowned Chhatrapati in 1674?
questions.exp: Shivaji was crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad in 1674, founding the Maratha kingdom.

questions.q: What is the minimum age for a citizen to vote in elections in India?
questions.exp: Every Indian citizen aged 18 or above can vote under universal adult franchise.

questions.q: How many members of the Lok Sabha are elected from constituencies across India?
questions.exp: The Lok Sabha has 543 members elected from 543 parliamentary constituencies.

questions.q: Which European sailor reached Calicut in 1498 by the sea route around Africa?
questions.exp: The Portuguese navigator Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in 1498, opening a sea route from Europe to India.

questions.q: A farmer's tractor is an example of which factor of production?
questions.exp: Tools and machines like a tractor are man-made goods used to produce other goods, i.e., physical capital.

questions.q: Which body conducts elections to Parliament and the state legislative assemblies in India?
questions.exp: The Election Commission of India is the independent constitutional body that conducts these elections.

questions.q: What was the Ashtapradhan in Shivaji's administration?
questions.c: A hill fort in the Western Ghats
questions.exp: 'Ashta' means eight; the Ashtapradhan was Shivaji's council of eight ministers who advised him.

questions.q: In India's parliamentary system, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to:
questions.exp: The government stays in power only while it has the confidence of the directly elected Lok Sabha.

questions.q: In a Lok Sabha constituency, candidate A gets 42,000 votes, B gets 38,000, C gets 25,000, and 5,000 voters choose NOTA. What is the result?
questions.a: No one wins, as nobody got over 50% of votes
questions.b: Candidate A wins, having the most votes
questions.c: The poll is cancelled because of NOTA votes
questions.d: A and B share the seat
questions.exp: India uses the first-past-the-post system: the candidate with the most votes wins, even without a majority; NOTA does not cancel the result.

questions.q: After the Battle of Buxar (1764), the East India Company received the diwani (right to collect revenue) of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa in 1765 from which ruler?
questions.exp: The Mughal emperor Shah Alam II granted the diwani to the Company by the Treaty of Allahabad in 1765.

questions.q: 'फल' शब्दस्य प्रथमाविभक्तौ बहुवचने रूपं किम्?
questions.exp: अकारान्त नपुंसकलिंग 'फल' का प्रथमा बहुवचन 'फलानि' होता है।

questions.q: 'गम्' धातोः लट्लकारे उत्तमपुरुषे एकवचने रूपं किम्?
questions.exp: उत्तम पुरुष एकवचन (अहम्) के साथ 'गच्छामि' रूप आता है।

questions.q: सप्ताहे कति दिनानि भवन्ति?
questions.exp: सप्ताह में सात दिन होते हैं; सात को संस्कृत में 'सप्त' कहते हैं।

questions.q: 'लता' शब्दस्य तृतीयाविभक्तौ एकवचने रूपं किम्?
questions.exp: आकारान्त स्त्रीलिंग 'लता' का तृतीया एकवचन 'लतया' होता है।

questions.q: उचितम् अव्ययपदं चिनुत: 'अहं ___ (आगामिनि दिने) विद्यालयं गमिष्यामि।'
questions.exp: 'श्वः' का अर्थ 'आने वाला कल' है और वाक्य भविष्यत्काल (गमिष्यामि) में है।

questions.q: 'पठितुम्' इति पदे कः प्रत्ययः अस्ति?
questions.exp: 'पठ् + तुमुन्' से 'पठितुम्' (पढ़ने के लिए) बनता है।

questions.q: उचितपदेन रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत: 'छात्राः ___ बहिः गच्छन्ति।'
questions.exp: 'बहिः' के योग में पंचमी विभक्ति होती है, अतः 'ग्रामात्' सही है।

questions.q: 'सः अपठत्' इति वाक्ये कः लकारः प्रयुक्तः?
questions.exp: 'अपठत्' भूतकाल का रूप है, जो लङ् लकार में बनता है।

questions.q: 'महोत्सवः' इति पदस्य सन्धिविच्छेदः कः?
questions.exp: आ + उ = ओ (गुण संधि), अतः महा + उत्सवः = महोत्सवः।

questions.q: अधोलिखितेषु वाक्येषु शुद्धं वाक्यं किम्?
questions.exp: 'वयम्' (उत्तम पुरुष बहुवचन) के साथ 'क्रीडामः' सही है; अन्य वाक्यों में कर्ता और क्रिया के पुरुष/वचन मेल नहीं खाते।

questions.q: In painting with pigments, which are the three primary colours?
questions.exp: Red, yellow and blue cannot be made by mixing other pigments, so they are the primary colours.

questions.q: Bharatanatyam is a classical dance form that developed in which state?
questions.exp: Bharatanatyam originated in Tamil Nadu; Odissi, Manipuri and Sattriya belong to the other states.

questions.q: Madhubani (Mithila) painting is a folk art tradition of which state?
questions.exp: Madhubani painting comes from the Mithila region of Bihar.

questions.q: Which of these is a string instrument?
questions.exp: The sitar produces sound from plucked strings; tabla is a drum and bansuri and shehnai are wind instruments.

questions.q: When white is added to a colour to make it lighter, the result is called a:
questions.exp: Adding white gives a tint; adding black gives a shade and adding grey gives a tone.

questions.q: To show depth in a landscape drawing, trees that are far away should be drawn:
questions.c: In sharper detail than nearby trees
questions.d: Exactly the same size as nearby trees
questions.exp: In perspective drawing, distant objects appear smaller (and less detailed), which creates a sense of depth.

questions.q: In a play, what is a monologue?
questions.b: A song sung by the whole group
questions.c: A long speech by a single character
questions.exp: 'Mono' means one; a monologue is an extended speech delivered by one character.

questions.q: In Indian music, what does 'tala' refer to?
questions.exp: Tala is the rhythmic cycle of a fixed number of beats that repeats through a composition.

questions.q: Kavya mixes equal amounts of red and green poster paint (complementary colours). What colour is she most likely to get?
questions.exp: Complementary pigments cancel each other's brightness when mixed, producing a dull brownish-grey.

questions.q: Teentaal has 16 beats divided into 4 equal sections (vibhags). How many beats are there in each vibhag?
questions.exp: 16 beats ÷ 4 vibhags = 4 beats in each vibhag.

questions.q: How many players of one team are on the field at a time in a football match?
questions.exp: Each football team plays with 11 players on the field, including the goalkeeper.

questions.q: How many interlocking rings are there in the Olympic symbol?
questions.exp: The Olympic symbol has five interlocking rings representing the union of the continents.

questions.q: Pranayama in yoga is mainly concerned with:
questions.exp: Pranayama consists of breathing practices that regulate inhalation, retention and exhalation.

questions.q: How many players of each team are on the court at a time in volleyball?
questions.exp: A volleyball team has six players on court at a time.

questions.q: How is Body Mass Index (BMI) calculated?
questions.exp: BMI = body weight in kilograms divided by the square of height in metres.

questions.q: Which activity best improves flexibility?
questions.b: Eating extra protein at every meal
questions.exp: Stretching increases the range of movement of joints and muscles, which is flexibility.

questions.q: Which describes correct sitting posture while studying?
questions.b: Back straight, shoulders relaxed, feet flat on floor
questions.c: Sitting on the chair's edge with legs crossed
questions.d: Resting the head on the desk
questions.exp: A straight back with relaxed shoulders and feet on the floor keeps the spine in its natural alignment.

questions.q: After losing a close match, what should a player with good sportsmanship do?
questions.b: Blame the referee loudly for the loss
questions.c: Refuse to attend the prize ceremony
questions.exp: Sportsmanship means respecting opponents and officials and accepting the result gracefully.

questions.q: Neha weighs 45 kg and is 1.5 m tall. What is her BMI?
Maximum heart rate is estimated as 220 − age. A 14-year-old wants to train at 70% of maximum heart rate. What is the approximate target heart rate?
questions.exp: Maximum = 220 − 14 = 206; 70% of 206 = 144.2, i.e. about 144 beats per minute.

questions.q: Which hand tool is used to tighten or loosen screws?
questions.exp: A screwdriver fits into the head of a screw and turns it.

questions.q: A place where seedlings and young plants are raised before transplanting is called a:
questions.exp: A nursery is where seeds are germinated and young plants are cared for until they are ready to plant out.

questions.q: Which product mainly comes from a dairy farm?
questions.exp: Dairy farms rear cows and buffaloes for milk; silk, honey and wool come from other animals.

questions.q: A lever, such as a see-saw, is an example of a:
questions.exp: A lever is a simple machine that helps lift loads with less effort.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of drip irrigation?
questions.a: Saves water by wetting only the roots
questions.exp: Drip irrigation delivers water drop by drop near the roots, so little is lost to evaporation or runoff.

questions.q: Sun-drying helps preserve mango slices mainly because it:
questions.b: Removes moisture that microbes need to grow
questions.exp: Microbes need water to grow; drying removes moisture and so slows spoilage.

questions.q: In a well-organised school library, books are usually arranged:
questions.a: By the colour of their covers
questions.b: By the size and thickness of each book
questions.d: In whatever order they were returned
questions.exp: A subject classification system (such as Dewey Decimal) keeps related books together so they are easy to find.

questions.q: Poultry farming involves rearing which of these (for eggs and meat)?
questions.exp: Poultry means domesticated birds such as chickens and ducks, reared for eggs and meat.

questions.q: A school garden uses 5000 L of water per day with flood irrigation. Drip irrigation would use 40% less water. How much water would be saved in 30 days?
Using a lever, the effort arm is 60 cm and the load arm is 20 cm. What effort is needed to lift a load of 150 N?
questions.exp: Effort × effort arm = load × load arm, so effort = 150 × 20 ÷ 60 = 50 N.

questions.q: Which of the following is a rational number lying between 1 and 2?
questions.exp: 3/2 = 1.5 can be written as p/q and lies between 1 and 2; √2 and √3 lie between 1 and 2 but are irrational, and 5/2 = 2.5 is greater than 2.

questions.q: Every point on the y-axis has coordinates of the form:
questions.exp: On the y-axis the distance from the y-axis (the x-coordinate) is zero, so points are (0, b).

questions.q: Two angles are complementary. If one of them is 35°, the other angle is:
questions.exp: Complementary angles add up to 90°, so the other angle = 90° − 35° = 55°.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a valid rule for proving two triangles congruent?
questions.exp: SAS, ASA (and AAS), SSS and RHS are congruence rules; two sides with a non-included angle (SSA) does not guarantee congruence.

questions.q: A bag contains 3 red balls and 5 blue balls. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is red?
questions.exp: There are 3 + 5 = 8 equally likely outcomes, of which 3 are red, so P(red) = 3/8.

questions.q: What is the 10th term of the arithmetic progression 3, 7, 11, 15, …?
questions.exp: a = 3, d = 4, so the 10th term = a + 9d = 3 + 36 = 39.

questions.q: Which of the following points lies on the line 2x − y = 4?
questions.exp: For (3, 2): 2(3) − 2 = 4 ✓. The others give 1, 0 and −4.

questions.q: In a parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = 70°. What is the measure of ∠B?
questions.exp: Adjacent angles of a parallelogram are supplementary, so ∠B = 180° − 70° = 110°.

questions.q: A chord of length 16 cm is drawn in a circle of radius 10 cm. What is the distance of the chord from the centre?
questions.exp: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, so distance = √(10² − 8²) = √(100 − 64) = √36 = 6 cm.

questions.q: If x + 1/x = 5, then the value of x² + 1/x² is:
Which of the following is a mixture?
questions.exp: Air contains nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide and other gases in no fixed ratio, so it is a mixture; the others are compounds.

questions.q: Which type of tissue is mainly responsible for movement in our body?
questions.exp: Muscle cells contain contractile proteins that contract and relax to cause movement.

questions.q: The SI unit of work is:
questions.exp: Work = force × displacement, measured in newton-metre, which is called a joule.

questions.q: Which structure is present in a plant cell but absent in an animal cell?
questions.exp: Plant cells have a rigid cellulose cell wall outside the cell membrane; animal cells do not.

questions.topic: Force and Laws of Motion — Momentum
questions.q: What is the momentum of a 2 kg ball moving with a velocity of 5 m/s?
questions.exp: Momentum p = mv = 2 kg × 5 m/s = 10 kg m/s.

questions.q: Which of the following will show the Tyndall effect when a beam of light is passed through it?
questions.exp: Milk is a colloid whose particles are large enough to scatter light; true solutions do not scatter light.

questions.q: An atom of sodium has atomic number 11 and mass number 23. How many neutrons does it have?
questions.exp: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 23 − 11 = 12.

questions.topic: Structure of the Atom — Electronic Configuration
questions.q: The electronic configuration (K, L, M shells) of chlorine (atomic number 17) is:
questions.exp: Shells fill in order K (max 2), L (max 8), then M gets the remaining 17 − 10 = 7 electrons.

questions.q: A boy claps near a tall wall and hears the echo after 2 s. If the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s, how far is the wall from him?
questions.exp: Sound travels to the wall and back: 2d = 340 × 2 = 680 m, so d = 340 m.

questions.q: A 50 kg boy runs up 15 steps, each 20 cm high, in 10 s. What power does he develop? (g = 10 m/s²)
Which place marks the southern tip of the Indian mainland?
questions.exp: Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu is the southernmost point of the Indian mainland (Indira Point, the southernmost point of India, is in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands).

questions.topic: History — Early Humans and Beginning of Civilisation
questions.q: The Great Bath, a large tank built of burnt bricks, was found at which Harappan city?
questions.exp: The Great Bath lies in the citadel area of Mohenjo-daro and was probably used for ritual bathing.

questions.q: In which layer of the atmosphere do almost all weather phenomena, such as clouds and rain, take place?
questions.exp: The troposphere is the lowest layer and contains almost all the water vapour and dust, so clouds, rain and storms occur there.

questions.q: The value of the next best alternative that is given up when a choice is made is called:
questions.exp: Because resources are scarce, choosing one option means giving up the next best one; that sacrifice is the opportunity cost.

questions.topic: Geography — Shaping of the Earth’s Surface
questions.q: The rigid outer shell of the Earth, made up of the crust and the uppermost mantle and broken into plates, is called the:
questions.exp: The lithosphere (crust + uppermost mantle) is broken into tectonic plates that move over the softer asthenosphere below.

questions.q: Under the First Past the Post (FPTP) system used in Lok Sabha elections, a candidate wins a constituency by:
questions.a: Getting more than half of all votes cast
questions.b: Getting more votes than any other candidate
questions.c: Winning seats in proportion to the party’s vote share
questions.d: Being nominated by the largest party
questions.exp: In FPTP the candidate with the highest number of votes wins, even without a majority; seats in proportion to vote share is proportional representation.

questions.q: Which body conducts elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies in India?
questions.exp: The Election Commission is an independent constitutional body that supervises and conducts these elections.

questions.topic: Economics — The Price Puzzle: What Drives the Market
questions.q: Other things remaining the same, when the price of a good rises, the quantity demanded of it usually:
questions.exp: By the law of demand, price and quantity demanded move in opposite directions, so a higher price reduces the quantity demanded.

questions.q: A region has an area of 2,00,000 km² and a population of 5 crore. What is its population density?
questions.exp: Density = population ÷ area = 5,00,00,000 ÷ 2,00,000 = 250 persons per km².

questions.topic: Economics — The Price Puzzle: What Drives the Market
questions.q: At a price of ₹40 per kg, buyers in a market want 500 kg of tomatoes but sellers offer only 300 kg. What is most likely to happen next?
questions.a: The price will rise until demand and supply become equal
questions.b: The price will fall to attract more buyers
questions.c: Nothing, as the market is already in equilibrium
questions.d: Sellers will reduce the quantity they offer
questions.exp: There is excess demand (a shortage) of 200 kg, so buyers bid up the price; a higher price lowers demand and raises supply until they are equal at equilibrium.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to 'ancient'.
questions.exp: 'Ancient' means very old; its opposite is 'modern'. 'Old' and 'antique' are near-synonyms.

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.exp: The correct spelling has one 'c' and double 's': n-e-c-e-s-s-a-r-y.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: She has been living in this city ______ 2019.
questions.exp: 'Since' is used with a point of time (2019) in the perfect continuous tense; 'for' is used with a period of time.

questions.q: Identify the adverb in the sentence: 'She sang the song beautifully.'
questions.exp: 'Beautifully' tells us how she sang, so it modifies the verb and is an adverb.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Neither the teacher nor the students ______ present in the hall.
questions.exp: With 'neither…nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject; 'students' is plural and the sentence is in the past, so 'were'.

questions.q: Choose the conjunction that best completes the sentence: He was very tired, ______ he kept working.
questions.exp: 'Yet' shows contrast: he was tired, but still continued to work.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: There is ______ milk left in the jug, so please buy some more.
questions.exp: 'Milk' is uncountable, and the need to buy more shows 'hardly any', so 'little' fits; 'few/many/a few' go with countable nouns.

questions.q: Which figure of speech is used in: 'The wind whispered through the trees'?
questions.exp: The wind is given a human action (whispering), which is personification.

questions.q: Rearrange the words to form a meaningful sentence: always / honesty / the / is / best / policy
questions.a: Honesty is always the best policy.
questions.b: The best policy always is honesty.
questions.c: Honesty always is policy the best.
questions.d: Is honesty always the best policy policy.
questions.exp: Subject 'Honesty' + verb 'is' + adverb 'always' + complement 'the best policy' gives the correct order.

questions.q: Choose the correct option: If I ______ a bird, I would fly over the mountains.
questions.exp: An imaginary present situation uses 'If + past subjunctive (were) … would + verb'; 'had been' would need 'would have flown'.

questions.q: 'जल' का पर्यायवाची शब्द कौन-सा है?
questions.exp: 'नीर' का अर्थ पानी है; 'अनल' आग, 'अनिल' हवा और 'नभ' आकाश है।

questions.q: निम्नलिखित में से शुद्ध वर्तनी वाला शब्द चुनिए।
questions.exp: सही शब्द 'आशीर्वाद' है, जिसमें 'शी' दीर्घ है और 'र्' का रेफ 'वा' पर लगता है।

questions.q: 'स्वतंत्र' का विलोम शब्द है —
questions.exp: 'स्वतंत्र' का अर्थ है अपने अधीन; इसका उल्टा 'परतंत्र' (दूसरे के अधीन) है। बाकी विकल्प समानार्थी हैं।

questions.q: 'सूर्योदय' शब्द का सही संधि-विच्छेद है —
questions.exp: अ + उ = ओ (गुण संधि), इसलिए सूर्य + उदय = सूर्योदय।

questions.q: 'राजपुत्र' (राजा का पुत्र) में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.exp: विग्रह में 'का' (संबंध कारक) का लोप हुआ है और उत्तरपद प्रधान है, इसलिए यह तत्पुरुष समास है।

questions.q: 'नाक में दम करना' मुहावरे का अर्थ है —
questions.exp: 'नाक में दम करना' का अर्थ किसी को इतना तंग करना कि वह बेहाल हो जाए।

questions.q: 'वह लड़का बहुत ईमानदार है।' — इस वाक्य में विशेषण शब्द कौन-सा है?
questions.exp: 'ईमानदार' लड़के (संज्ञा) की विशेषता बताता है, इसलिए विशेषण है; 'बहुत' विशेषण की विशेषता बताने वाला प्रविशेषण है।

questions.q: 'मिठास' शब्द में कौन-सा प्रत्यय लगा है?
questions.exp: मीठा + आस = मिठास; यहाँ 'आस' प्रत्यय से भाववाचक संज्ञा बनी है।

questions.q: 'उसका मुख चंद्रमा के समान सुंदर है।' — इस पंक्ति में कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.exp: मुख (उपमेय) की तुलना चंद्रमा (उपमान) से 'समान' वाचक शब्द द्वारा की गई है, अतः उपमा अलंकार है।

questions.q: निम्नलिखित में से शुद्ध वाक्य कौन-सा है?
questions.d: मेरे को आज एक पुस्तक पढ़ी।
questions.exp: सकर्मक क्रिया के भूतकाल में कर्ता के साथ 'ने' आता है और क्रिया कर्म (पुस्तक — स्त्रीलिंग) के अनुसार 'पढ़ी' होती है।

questions.q: 'लता' शब्दस्य प्रथमा-विभक्तौ बहुवचने रूपम् अस्ति —
questions.exp: आकारान्त स्त्रीलिंग 'लता' के प्रथमा के रूप: लता, लते, लताः — अतः बहुवचन 'लताः' है।

questions.q: 'गम्' धातोः लट्लकारे उत्तमपुरुषे एकवचने रूपम् अस्ति —
questions.exp: लट् उत्तमपुरुष एकवचन (मैं जाता हूँ) = गच्छामि; गच्छामः बहुवचन है।

questions.q: 'पञ्च' इति सङ्ख्या अङ्केषु का?
questions.exp: 'पञ्च' का अर्थ पाँच (५) है; सप्त = ७, नव = ९, चत्वारि = ४।

questions.q: 'फलम्' इति शब्दः कस्मिन् लिङ्गे अस्ति?
questions.exp: 'फलम्' अकारान्त नपुंसकलिंग शब्द है (फलम्, फले, फलानि)।

questions.q: 'अपठत्' इति पदं कस्मिन् लकारे अस्ति?
questions.exp: धातु से पहले 'अ' लगना और 'त्' अंत लङ्लकार (भूतकाल) का चिह्न है: अपठत् = उसने पढ़ा।

questions.q: उचितं पदं चिनुत — ________ परितः वृक्षाः सन्ति। (ग्राम)
questions.exp: 'परितः' (चारों ओर) के योग में द्वितीया विभक्ति होती है, अतः 'ग्रामम्'।

questions.q: 'महा + ईशः' इत्यनयोः सन्धिः भवति —
questions.exp: आ + ई = ए (गुण सन्धि), इसलिए महा + ईशः = महेशः।

questions.q: 'ह्यः' इति अव्ययस्य विपरीतार्थकं पदम् अस्ति —
questions.exp: 'ह्यः' का अर्थ बीता हुआ कल है और 'श्वः' का अर्थ आने वाला कल, अतः ये विपरीतार्थक हैं।

questions.q: उचितं क्रियापदं चिनुत — त्वं पाठं ________। (पठ्, लोट्लकारः)
questions.exp: कर्ता 'त्वम्' मध्यमपुरुष एकवचन है; लोट् मध्यमपुरुष एकवचन रूप 'पठ' है। पठतु प्रथमपुरुष, पठानि उत्तमपुरुष और पठथ लट् का रूप है।

questions.q: उचितं क्रियापदं चिनुत — वयं क्रीडाक्षेत्रे ________।
questions.exp: 'वयम्' उत्तमपुरुष बहुवचन है, अतः क्रिया भी उत्तमपुरुष बहुवचन 'क्रीडामः' होगी।

questions.q: The LCM of 12 and 18 is:
The quadratic equation x² − 6x + 9 = 0 has:
questions.exp: Discriminant D = b² − 4ac = 36 − 36 = 0, so the roots are real and equal (x = 3).

questions.q: The value of tan 45° is:
The distance of the point (3, 4) from the origin is:
questions.exp: Distance = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 units.

questions.topic: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
questions.q: The pair of equations 2x + 3y = 5 and 4x + 6y = 10 has:
questions.exp: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂ = 1/2, so the lines are coincident and have infinitely many solutions.

questions.q: The sum of the first 10 terms of the AP 2, 5, 8, 11, … is:
A fair die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a prime number?
questions.exp: Prime outcomes are 2, 3 and 5, i.e. 3 out of 6, so P = 3/6 = 1/2.

questions.q: The corresponding sides of two similar triangles are in the ratio 4 : 9. The ratio of their areas is:
questions.exp: The ratio of areas of similar triangles equals the square of the ratio of corresponding sides: 4² : 9² = 16 : 81.

questions.q: A solid clay cone of height 24 cm and base radius 6 cm is reshaped into a sphere. What is the radius of the sphere?
questions.exp: Volumes are equal: (1/3)π × 6² × 24 = (4/3)πr³ → 288 = (4/3)r³ → r³ = 216 → r = 6 cm.

questions.q: For a distribution, the mode is 24 and the mean is 30. Using the empirical relation 3 Median = Mode + 2 Mean, the median is:
Which gas is released when zinc granules react with dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.exp: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂; the gas burns with a pop sound.

questions.q: The common name of calcium oxychloride (CaOCl₂) is:
questions.exp: Bleaching powder is made by passing chlorine over dry slaked lime; baking soda is NaHCO₃ and washing soda Na₂CO₃·10H₂O.

questions.q: Which part of the brain maintains posture and balance of the body?
questions.exp: The cerebellum in the hind-brain controls precision of voluntary actions, posture and balance.

questions.q: The SI unit of the power of a lens is:
questions.exp: Power P = 1/f (in metres); 1 dioptre is the power of a lens of focal length 1 m.

questions.q: What is the power of a concave lens of focal length 50 cm?
questions.exp: For a concave lens f = −50 cm = −0.5 m, so P = 1/f = 1/(−0.5) = −2 D.

questions.q: Which compound is the next member after methane (CH₄) in its homologous series?
questions.exp: Successive members of the alkane series differ by CH₂, so CH₄ + CH₂ = C₂H₆ (ethane).

questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: The sky appears blue on a clear day mainly because of:
questions.b: scattering of light by fine particles in air
questions.d: reflection of light from the surface of the sea
questions.exp: Tiny air molecules scatter shorter (blue) wavelengths much more than red, so scattered blue light reaches our eyes.

questions.q: Which organism commonly reproduces asexually by budding?
questions.exp: Hydra forms a bud that grows into a new individual; Plasmodium shows multiple fission, Planaria regeneration and Spirogyra fragmentation.

questions.q: A 1000 W electric iron is used for 2 hours daily for 30 days. If 1 unit (kWh) costs ₹5, what is the cost of electricity?
questions.exp: Energy = 1 kW × 2 h × 30 = 60 kWh; cost = 60 × ₹5 = ₹300.

questions.q: Element X forms an oxide X₂O₃ that reacts with both hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide to form salt and water. X is most likely:
questions.exp: Al₂O₃ is an amphoteric oxide reacting with both acids and bases; Na₂O and CuO are basic and sulphur forms acidic oxides (not X₂O₃).

Social Science — History.book: India and the Contemporary World II

questions.topic: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
questions.q: Which French artist prepared a series of four prints in 1848 visualising a world of 'democratic and social Republics'?
questions.exp: Frédéric Sorrieu's prints show peoples of Europe and America marching past the Statue of Liberty, expressing his utopian vision.

questions.q: In which year did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre take place in Amritsar?
questions.exp: On 13 April 1919 General Dyer ordered troops to fire on an unarmed crowd gathered in Jallianwala Bagh.

questions.topic: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
questions.q: Who founded the secret society 'Young Italy'?
questions.exp: Mazzini founded Young Italy in Marseilles in 1831 to spread the idea of a unified Italian republic.

questions.q: Which book, written by Mahatma Gandhi, declared that British rule survived in India only because of Indians' cooperation?
questions.exp: In Hind Swaraj (1909) Gandhiji argued that if Indians refused to cooperate, British rule would collapse within a year.

questions.q: The Poona Pact of September 1932 was an agreement between:
questions.b: Jawaharlal Nehru and Muhammad Ali Jinnah
questions.c: Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
questions.exp: The Poona Pact gave the Depressed Classes reserved seats in legislatures but to be voted in by the general electorate.

questions.topic: The Making of a Global World
questions.q: Which two institutions were set up at the Bretton Woods conference in 1944?
questions.exp: The Bretton Woods conference created the International Monetary Fund and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (World Bank).

questions.topic: Print Culture and the Modern World
questions.q: The earliest kind of print technology, hand printing with wooden blocks, was developed in:
questions.exp: From about AD 594 books in China were printed by rubbing paper against inked wooden blocks; the technique later reached Japan.

questions.q: Who were the 'gomasthas' in the context of the Indian textile trade?
questions.a: Rich Indian merchants who exported cloth
questions.b: Master weavers who owned many looms
questions.d: Paid servants of the East India Company who supervised weavers
questions.exp: The Company appointed gomasthas to supervise weavers, collect supplies and check the quality of cloth.

questions.topic: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
questions.q: Poets and artists of Europe supported this country's struggle for independence, calling it the cradle of European civilisation. It was recognised as an independent nation by the Treaty of Constantinople, 1832. Which country is this?
questions.exp: The Greek war of independence against the Ottoman Empire began in 1821 and ended with the Treaty of Constantinople in 1832.

questions.q: In 1921 many plantation workers in Assam left the tea gardens saying they were going home under 'Gandhi Raj'. Which law did they defy by doing so?
questions.exp: The Inland Emigration Act of 1859 did not allow plantation workers to leave the tea gardens without permission.

questions.q: Which is the most widely spread and important soil in India?
questions.exp: Alluvial soil, deposited by the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra systems, covers the entire northern plains and parts of the east coast.

questions.q: 'Slash and burn' agriculture is a type of:
questions.exp: Farmers clear a patch of forest by burning, grow crops with simple tools for family needs and then shift to a new patch.

questions.q: Which type of coal is the highest quality hard coal with the highest carbon content?
questions.exp: Anthracite is formed under the greatest heat and pressure and has the most carbon; peat has the least.

questions.q: Which of the following is a rabi crop?
questions.exp: Rabi crops are sown in winter (October–December) and harvested in summer; wheat is the main rabi crop.

questions.q: The iron and steel industry is called a 'basic industry' because:
questions.a: it uses only agricultural raw materials from Indian farms and forests
questions.b: it is owned only by the government
questions.c: it produces goods only for export
questions.d: other industries depend on it for machinery and raw material
questions.exp: Heavy, medium and light industries all depend on iron and steel for their machinery and materials.

questions.q: The Bhakra Nangal project is built on which river?
questions.exp: The Bhakra Nangal dam is on the Sutlej and its water is shared by Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan.

questions.q: Land in the Chambal basin made unfit for cultivation by deep gullies is called:
questions.exp: Running water cuts deep channels (gullies) in clayey soils; such land in the Chambal basin is called bad land (ravines).

questions.q: The monazite sands of Kerala are rich in which mineral used for nuclear energy?
questions.exp: Monazite sands of Kerala contain thorium, an atomic mineral used to generate nuclear power.

questions.q: Rice is a commercial crop in Punjab and Haryana, but a subsistence crop in Odisha. What does this show?
questions.a: Rice grows only in eastern India
questions.b: The degree of commercialisation of a crop varies from region to region
questions.c: Punjab and Haryana do not eat rice, so they sell all of it
questions.exp: The same crop may be grown for sale in one region and for the family's own use in another.

questions.q: A country has a total reporting area of 300 million hectares, of which 141 million hectares is net sown area. What percentage of its area is net sown?
In Belgium, the 'community government' is elected by people belonging to:
questions.exp: The community government is elected by people of one language community (Dutch, French or German-speaking) and handles cultural, educational and language issues.

questions.q: Subjects like education, forests, trade unions and marriage are included in which list?
questions.exp: These subjects are of common interest, so both the Union and State governments can make laws on them.

questions.q: Which of the following is a recognised national political party in India?
questions.exp: The BJP is recognised as a national party; DMK, Shiv Sena and BJD are state parties.

questions.q: Who is the elected head of a gram panchayat?
questions.exp: The gram panchayat is headed by a president called the sarpanch; a mayor heads a municipal corporation.

questions.q: Which country is an example of a 'coming together' federation?
questions.exp: In the USA independent states came together to form a bigger unit; India, Spain and Belgium are 'holding together' federations.

questions.q: Power shared among the legislature, executive and judiciary is called:
questions.exp: The organs are at the same level and check each other, so it is horizontal sharing, also called checks and balances.

questions.q: A system that values men more and gives them power over women is called:
questions.exp: Patriarchy literally means rule by the father; feminism is the movement for equal rights for women.

questions.q: What is the main aim of the anti-defection law in India?
questions.a: To ban small regional parties from contesting any elections
questions.d: To stop elected MLAs and MPs from changing parties
questions.exp: An MLA or MP who changes party after being elected loses the seat, which checks defection for money or office.

questions.q: In Country X, the central government has an equal number of ministers from the two main language groups, and the capital city has a separate government with equal representation. Which country follows this model?
questions.exp: Belgium's constitution has equal Dutch and French-speaking ministers and a separate Brussels government with equal representation.

questions.q: A new subject such as computer software is not mentioned in the Union, State or Concurrent List. Who can make laws on it?
questions.exp: Subjects not in any list are residuary subjects, and the Union Government has the power to legislate on them.

questions.q: The primary sector is also called the:
questions.exp: Activities that directly use natural resources, like farming, dairy and fishing, form the primary sector, also called agriculture and related sector.

questions.q: The main aim of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) is to:
questions.exp: The WTO was set up to liberalise international trade by making rules and removing trade barriers.

questions.q: Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) indicates the number of children who die:
questions.a: before age five, per 1,00,000 live births
questions.d: before age one, per 1000 live births
questions.exp: IMR = number of children dying before the age of one year as a proportion of 1000 live children born in that year.

questions.q: An asset owned by a borrower that is used as a guarantee to a lender until the loan is repaid is called:
questions.exp: Collateral such as land, a building or livestock can be sold by the lender if the borrower fails to repay.

questions.q: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the value of:
questions.a: all goods and services produced in a year, including intermediate goods
questions.b: only goods exported in a year
questions.c: all final goods and services produced within a country in a year
questions.d: all goods produced by the government only
questions.exp: Only final goods and services are counted to avoid double counting of intermediate goods.

questions.topic: Money and Credit — Self Help Groups
questions.q: A typical Self Help Group (SHG) in rural India has about:
questions.exp: An SHG usually has 15–20 members, mostly women, from one locality who pool their savings.

questions.q: A multinational corporation (MNC) is a company that:
questions.a: owns or controls production in more than one nation
questions.b: sells goods only within the country where it is registered
questions.c: is owned by many state governments
questions.d: only imports goods from other countries
questions.exp: MNCs set up factories and offices in several countries where they can get cheap labour and other resources.

questions.q: Overuse of which resource is the clearest threat to sustainable development, since it cannot be replenished?
questions.exp: Crude oil is non-renewable and will get exhausted after years of use; solar, wind and tidal energy are renewable.

questions.topic: Money and Credit — Terms of Credit
questions.q: A moneylender gives Shyam a loan of ₹10,000 at 3% simple interest per month. How much interest will Shyam pay for one year?
questions.exp: Interest per month = 3% of ₹10,000 = ₹300; for 12 months = ₹300 × 12 = ₹3,600 (36% a year).

questions.q: In a country, the primary sector employs 60% of workers but produces only 20% of GDP. What does this most likely indicate?
questions.c: The primary sector is the largest producer
questions.exp: More workers than needed share a small output, so each works below potential — disguised unemployment or underemployment.

questions.q: Who is the poet of 'Dust of Snow'?
questions.exp: 'Dust of Snow' (and 'Fire and Ice') were written by the American poet Robert Frost.

questions.topic: From the Diary of Anne Frank (First Flight)
questions.q: What name did Anne Frank give to her diary?
questions.exp: Anne called her diary 'Kitty' and wrote to it as if to a friend; Margot was her sister.

questions.q: In 'The Hundred Dresses', which girl claims she has a hundred dresses at home?
questions.exp: Wanda, a poor Polish girl who wore the same faded dress daily, said she had a hundred dresses at home.

questions.q: Who is the eight-year-old girl who takes a secret bus ride to the town in 'Madam Rides the Bus'?
questions.exp: Valliammai (Valli) saved coins for months to ride the bus to the town and back.

questions.topic: A Triumph of Surgery (Footprints without Feet)
questions.q: Why did Tricki, the dog, fall ill in 'A Triumph of Surgery'?
questions.a: He was bitten by another dog
questions.b: He caught an infection from other dogs in the street
questions.c: He was left alone and starved
questions.d: He was overfed and got too little exercise
questions.exp: Mrs Pumphrey pampered Tricki with too much rich food and sweets and gave him little exercise.

questions.q: According to one story in 'Coorg', the people of Coorg are descended from:
questions.a: soldiers of the Mughal emperor Akbar
questions.exp: One story says a part of Alexander's army settled in Coorg, which is why the people are said to be of Greek or Arabic descent.

questions.q: In Robert Frost's 'Fire and Ice', what does 'ice' symbolise?
questions.exp: Fire stands for desire (greed, lust) and ice stands for hatred, cold and rigid, both of which can destroy the world.

questions.q: From whom did Matilda borrow the diamond necklace for the ball?
questions.exp: Matilda borrowed the necklace from her rich friend Mrs (Madame) Forestier; it later turned out to be fake.

questions.q: Griffin made himself invisible, then set fire to his landlord's house and robbed shops and an inn. Which description fits him best?
questions.a: A kind scientist who used invisibility to help the poor
questions.d: A brilliant scientist but a lawless person
questions.exp: Griffin was a gifted scientist who discovered invisibility, but he used it for revenge and theft, showing a lawless nature.

questions.q: In 'The Ball Poem', what is the main lesson the boy learns from losing his ball?
questions.a: Everyone must learn to bear loss and stand up again
questions.b: He should immediately buy a new ball with his own money
questions.c: Balls must never be played with near water
questions.d: His parents will always replace what he loses
questions.exp: The poet says money is external; the boy must learn the 'epistemology of loss' — how to accept loss and move on.

questions.q: 'लखनवी अंदाज़' पाठ के लेखक कौन हैं?
questions.exp: 'लखनवी अंदाज़' यशपाल की रचना है, जिसमें नवाब साहब के खीरा खाने के दिखावटी अंदाज़ पर व्यंग्य है।

questions.q: 'बड़े भाई साहब' कहानी के लेखक कौन हैं?
questions.exp: 'बड़े भाई साहब' मुंशी प्रेमचंद की प्रसिद्ध कहानी है।

questions.q: 'साना-साना हाथ जोड़ि' यात्रा-वृत्तांत की लेखिका कौन हैं?
questions.exp: यह सिक्किम यात्रा पर आधारित मधु कांकरिया का यात्रा-वृत्तांत है।

questions.q: 'चरण-कमल बंदौं हरि राई' — इस पंक्ति में कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.exp: यहाँ उपमेय 'चरण' पर उपमान 'कमल' का अभेद आरोप किया गया है (चरण ही कमल हैं), अतः रूपक अलंकार है।

questions.q: 'राम-लक्ष्मण-परशुराम संवाद' किस कवि की रचना से लिया गया है?
questions.exp: यह अंश तुलसीदास के 'रामचरितमानस' के बालकांड से लिया गया है।

questions.q: 'बच्चा धीरे-धीरे चलता है।' — इस वाक्य में 'धीरे-धीरे' का पद परिचय है —
questions.exp: 'धीरे-धीरे' बताता है कि क्रिया 'चलना' किस ढंग से हो रही है, इसलिए यह रीतिवाचक क्रियाविशेषण है।

questions.q: सूरदास के पदों में गोपियाँ उद्धव को 'बड़भागी' कहकर क्या व्यक्त करती हैं?
questions.a: सच्ची प्रशंसा, क्योंकि उद्धव बहुत ज्ञानी और योगी पुरुष हैं
questions.b: व्यंग्य, क्योंकि कृष्ण के पास रहकर भी वे प्रेम से अछूते हैं
questions.c: आभार, क्योंकि वे कृष्ण का संदेश लाए
questions.d: डर, क्योंकि वे राजा के मित्र हैं
questions.exp: गोपियाँ व्यंग्य करती हैं कि उद्धव कृष्ण के निकट रहकर भी उनके प्रेम-बंधन से अछूते रहे, जैसे कमल का पत्ता जल में रहकर भी गीला नहीं होता।

questions.topic: व्याकरण — रचना के आधार पर वाक्य-भेद
questions.q: 'सूरज निकला और अँधेरा दूर हो गया।' — रचना के आधार पर यह कौन-सा वाक्य है?
questions.exp: दो स्वतंत्र उपवाक्य समानाधिकरण योजक 'और' से जुड़े हैं, इसलिए यह संयुक्त वाक्य है।

questions.q: 'सोहत ओढ़े पीत पट, स्याम सलोने गात। मनहुँ नीलमनि सैल पर, आतप पर्यो प्रभात॥' — इन पंक्तियों में कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.exp: पीला वस्त्र ओढ़े श्याम शरीर में नीलमणि पर्वत पर सुबह की धूप पड़ने की संभावना 'मनहुँ' वाचक शब्द द्वारा व्यक्त की गई है, अतः उत्प्रेक्षा अलंकार है।

questions.q: लोककथा के अनुसार तताँरा द्वारा तलवार से धरती चीर देने पर कौन-से दो द्वीप बने?
questions.exp: कथा के अनुसार क्रोध में तताँरा ने तलवार धरती में गाड़कर खींची, जिससे द्वीप दो टुकड़ों — लिटिल अंदमान और कार-निकोबार — में बँट गया।

questions.q: 'हिम + आलयः' इत्यनयोः सन्धिः भवति —
questions.exp: अ + आ = आ (दीर्घ सन्धि), अतः हिम + आलयः = हिमालयः।

questions.q: 'पठ् + तुमुन्' इति योगेन पदं भवति —
questions.exp: तुमुन् प्रत्यय 'के लिए' अर्थ में लगता है: पठ् + तुमुन् = पठितुम् (पढ़ने के लिए)। पठित्वा क्त्वा से और पठितवान् क्तवतु से बनता है।

questions.q: 'सुखम्' इति पदस्य विलोमपदम् अस्ति —
questions.exp: 'सुखम्' का विलोम 'दुःखम्' है; हर्ष, आनन्द और मोद इसके समानार्थी हैं।

questions.q: 'पीताम्बरः' (पीतम् अम्बरं यस्य सः — कृष्णः) इत्यत्र कः समासः?
questions.exp: यहाँ दोनों पद मिलकर किसी अन्य (कृष्ण) का बोध कराते हैं, अतः बहुव्रीहि समास है।

questions.q: 9:45 इति समयः संस्कृते कथं लिख्यते?
questions.exp: 9:45 में दस बजने में पौना (एक चौथाई कम) है, अतः 'पादोनदशवादनम्'; पादोननववादनम् = 8:45।

questions.q: 'बालिका' इति पदे कः स्त्रीप्रत्ययः अस्ति?
questions.exp: बालक + टाप् = बालिका; ङीप् से 'नदी, देवी' जैसे ईकारान्त शब्द बनते हैं, मतुप् और त्व स्त्रीप्रत्यय नहीं हैं।

questions.q: 'रामलक्ष्मणौ' इति समस्तपदस्य विग्रहः अस्ति —
questions.exp: दोनों पद प्रधान हैं और 'च' से जुड़े हैं, अतः यह द्वन्द्व समास है: रामः च लक्ष्मणः च।

questions.q: 'नमः + ते' इत्यनयोः सन्धिः भवति —
questions.exp: विसर्ग के बाद 'त्' आने पर विसर्ग का 'स्' हो जाता है: नमः + ते = नमस्ते।

questions.q: उचितं पदं चिनुत — बालकः ________ बिभेति। (सिंह)
questions.exp: 'भी' (डरना) धातु के योग में भय के कारण में पञ्चमी विभक्ति होती है, अतः 'सिंहात्'।

questions.q: उचितं क्रियापदं चिनुत — श्वः अहं मातुलगृहं ________। (गम्)
questions.exp: 'श्वः' (आने वाला कल) से भविष्यकाल अर्थात् लृट्लकार, और कर्ता 'अहम्' उत्तमपुरुष एकवचन है: गमिष्यामि।

questions.q: How many significant figures are there in the measured value 0.007020 m?
questions.exp: Leading zeros are not significant; the digits 7, 0, 2 and the trailing 0 after the decimal are significant, giving 4.

questions.q: The tendency of a body to resist any change in its state of rest or of uniform motion is called:
questions.exp: Newton's first law describes inertia, the property of a body to resist change in its state of motion.

questions.q: The SI unit of specific heat capacity is:
questions.exp: Specific heat capacity s = Q/(m ΔT), so its unit is J per kg per K.

questions.q: Sound waves travelling through air are:
questions.exp: In air, particles oscillate along the direction of propagation through compressions and rarefactions, so sound is a longitudinal mechanical wave.

questions.q: If g is the acceleration due to gravity at the Earth's surface, its value at a height equal to the Earth's radius R above the surface is:
questions.exp: g(h) = g R²/(R + h)². With h = R, g(h) = g R²/(2R)² = g/4.

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A spinning ice skater pulls her arms close to her body and starts spinning faster. This happens because:
questions.a: Angular momentum is conserved while her inertia falls
questions.b: Her moment of inertia increases, so she spins faster
questions.c: Gravity exerts an extra torque on her body
questions.d: Friction from the ice supplies an extra torque
questions.exp: No external torque acts, so L = Iω is constant; pulling the arms in reduces I, so ω increases.

questions.q: If the absolute temperature of an ideal gas is made four times, the rms speed of its molecules becomes:
questions.exp: v_rms = √(3RT/M) ∝ √T, so increasing T by 4 times increases v_rms by √4 = 2 times.

questions.q: A force F = (3i + 4j) N displaces a body by d = (2i − j) m. The work done by the force is:
A wire of length 2 m and cross-sectional area 1 mm² stretches by 1 mm when a load of 100 N is hung from it. The Young's modulus of the material is:
A particle executes SHM given by x = 0.05 sin(4πt) metre. Its maximum speed and time period are:
questions.exp: ω = 4π rad/s, so T = 2π/ω = 0.5 s and v_max = Aω = 0.05 × 4π ≈ 0.63 m/s.

questions.q: The number of atoms present in exactly 12 g of carbon-12 is:
questions.exp: 12 g of C-12 is one mole, which contains the Avogadro number (6.022 × 10^23) of atoms.

questions.q: Which quantum number determines the shape of an orbital?
questions.exp: The azimuthal quantum number l defines the subshell (s, p, d, f) and hence the shape of the orbital.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which element has the highest electronegativity on the Pauling scale?
questions.exp: Fluorine is small with a high effective nuclear charge; it has the highest electronegativity (4.0).

questions.q: The hybridisation of each carbon atom in ethyne (HC≡CH) is:
questions.exp: Each carbon in ethyne forms two σ bonds and is linear (180°), which corresponds to sp hybridisation.

questions.q: Which of the following is an intensive property?
questions.exp: Temperature does not depend on the amount of matter, whereas volume, mass and enthalpy do.

questions.q: For N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g), ΔH < 0, the yield of ammonia at equilibrium can be increased by:
questions.exp: By Le Chatelier's principle, higher pressure favours the side with fewer gas moles (2 vs 4); a catalyst does not shift equilibrium.

questions.q: In the reaction Zn(s) + CuSO4(aq) → ZnSO4(aq) + Cu(s), the species that is oxidised is:
questions.exp: Zn loses two electrons (oxidation number 0 → +2), so zinc is oxidised while Cu²⁺ is reduced.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.q: Which carbocation is the most stable?
questions.exp: The tertiary carbocation is stabilised most by the +I effect and hyperconjugation of three methyl groups.

questions.q: Ozonolysis of but-2-ene (CH3-CH=CH-CH3) followed by treatment with Zn/H2O gives:
questions.exp: The C=C bond is cleaved and each half becomes CH3CHO, so two ethanal molecules form; Zn prevents oxidation to acids.

questions.q: 4 g of NaOH (molar mass 40 g/mol) is dissolved in water to make 250 mL of solution. The molarity of the solution is:
questions.exp: Moles = 4/40 = 0.1 mol; molarity = 0.1 mol ÷ 0.250 L = 0.4 M.

questions.q: The system of binomial nomenclature was given by:
questions.exp: Linnaeus introduced the two-part (genus + species) naming system for organisms.

questions.q: The dominant phase in the life cycle of bryophytes is the:
questions.exp: In bryophytes the main plant body is the haploid gametophyte; the sporophyte depends on it.

questions.q: The building blocks (monomers) of proteins are:
questions.exp: Proteins are polymers of amino acids joined by peptide bonds.

questions.q: Which part of the human heart acts as the pacemaker?
questions.exp: The sino-atrial node generates the maximum number of action potentials per minute and initiates each heartbeat.

questions.q: In a hypogynous flower (for example, mustard), the ovary is:
questions.exp: In hypogynous flowers the gynoecium is at the highest position and other floral parts arise below it, so the ovary is superior.

questions.q: Casparian strips are found in which layer of the root?
questions.exp: Endodermal cells have suberin-rich Casparian strips on their radial and tangential walls, blocking the apoplast path.

questions.q: During contraction of a skeletal muscle fibre, the length of which band remains unchanged?
questions.exp: Thin filaments slide over thick filaments; the A band (length of thick filaments) stays the same while the I band and H zone shorten.

questions.q: The oxygen released during photosynthesis comes from:
questions.exp: O2 is produced by photolysis (splitting) of water near Photosystem II.

questions.q: A diploid cell of an organism has 16 chromosomes. After the cell completes meiosis, the result is:
questions.exp: Meiosis produces four haploid cells, so each has 16 ÷ 2 = 8 chromosomes.

questions.q: A sugarcane farmer sprays a plant hormone on his crop, and the stems grow longer, increasing the yield by as much as 20 tonnes per acre. The hormone used is most likely:
questions.exp: Gibberellins cause stem (internode) elongation; spraying them on sugarcane increases stem length and yield.

questions.q: If A = {1, 2} and B = {3, 4, 5}, the number of elements in A × B is:
π/3 radians is equal to:
If A = {1, 2, 3, 4} and B = {3, 4, 5}, then A ∩ B is:
questions.exp: The intersection contains elements common to both sets: 3 and 4.

questions.q: The solution of 3x − 5 < 7, where x is a real number, is:
questions.exp: 3x − 5 < 7 ⇒ 3x < 12 ⇒ x < 4 (strict inequality).

questions.q: The value of (1 + i)² is:
In how many ways can a team of 3 students be chosen from 7 students?
questions.exp: Order does not matter: 7C3 = 7!/(3! 4!) = 35.

questions.q: The value of lim (x→2) (x² − 4)/(x − 2) is:
questions.exp: (x² − 4)/(x − 2) = x + 2 for x ≠ 2, so the limit is 2 + 2 = 4.

questions.q: The variance of the observations 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 is:
questions.exp: Mean = 6; squared deviations are 16, 4, 0, 4, 16, sum 40; variance = 40/5 = 8.

questions.q: The centre and radius of the circle x² + y² − 6x + 4y − 12 = 0 are:
A committee of 2 persons is to be chosen at random from 4 men and 3 women. What is the probability that both members are women?
Recording an asset in the books at the price paid to acquire it is based on the:
questions.exp: The cost (historical cost) concept requires assets to be recorded at their acquisition cost.

questions.q: Which of the following is an internal user of accounting information?
questions.exp: Management works inside the business and uses accounting information for planning and control.

questions.q: The source document prepared by a seller giving details of goods sold on credit is called a/an:
questions.exp: An invoice (bill) records quantity, price and value of goods sold and is the source document for credit sales.

questions.q: In the journal entry for rent paid in cash, the account debited is:
questions.exp: Rent is an expense; expenses are debited, and cash (asset) going out is credited.

questions.q: Goods purchased on credit are recorded in the:
questions.exp: Only credit purchases of goods meant for resale are entered in the Purchases Book.

questions.topic: Trial Balance and Rectification of Errors
questions.q: Purchase of machinery was wrongly debited to Purchases Account. This is an:
questions.exp: Treating a capital expenditure (machinery) as revenue expenditure (purchases) violates accounting principles.

questions.q: A firm has total assets of ₹1,50,000 and outside liabilities of ₹40,000. Its capital is:
questions.exp: Capital = Assets − Liabilities = 1,50,000 − 40,000 = ₹1,10,000.

questions.q: Which of the following is a charge against profit rather than an appropriation of profit?
questions.exp: Provisions are made for known liabilities or losses and must be charged before arriving at profit; reserves are appropriations.

questions.q: Cash Book shows a debit balance of ₹25,000. Cheques issued for ₹8,000 have not been presented for payment, and bank charges of ₹500 are not recorded in the Cash Book. The balance as per Pass Book is:
questions.exp: 25,000 + 8,000 (cheques not presented) − 500 (bank charges) = ₹32,500.

questions.q: A machine costing ₹50,000 is depreciated at 10% p.a. on the Written Down Value method. The depreciation for the third year is:
Which auxiliary to trade removes the hindrance of place?
questions.exp: Transport moves goods from the place of production to the place of consumption.

questions.q: The written agreement containing the terms of partnership is called the:
questions.exp: The partnership deed sets out capital, profit sharing, duties and other terms agreed by partners.

questions.q: A public enterprise set up by a special Act of Parliament or a State Legislature is a:
questions.exp: Statutory (public) corporations are created by a special Act that defines their powers and functions.

questions.q: The principle of insurance that requires the insured to have a financial interest in the subject matter is:
questions.exp: Insurable interest means the insured must suffer a financial loss if the subject matter is damaged.

questions.q: A company hands over its payroll processing and call-centre work to a specialist outside firm. This is an example of:
questions.exp: Contracting out non-core activities to outside agencies is outsourcing (business process outsourcing).

questions.q: Retained earnings as a source of finance are also known as:
questions.exp: Reinvesting a part of net profits in the business instead of distributing it is ploughing back of profits.

questions.q: Retailers who do not have a fixed place of business and move from place to place with their goods are called:
questions.exp: Itinerant retailers such as peddlers and hawkers keep moving to reach customers.

questions.q: A guarantee issued by the importer's bank promising payment up to a certain amount to the exporter is a:
questions.exp: A letter of credit assures the exporter that the importer's bank will honour payment.

questions.q: Small dairy farmers in a village form an organisation to collect their milk and sell it together directly to the market, avoiding middlemen. Each member has one vote. This organisation is a:
questions.exp: Producers who pool output to sell collectively and democratically (one member, one vote) form a marketing cooperative.

questions.q: A large company with a high credit rating needs funds for 90 days to meet a seasonal need. It issues an unsecured promissory note in the money market. This source is:
questions.exp: Commercial paper is an unsecured short-term promissory note (15 days to 1 year) issued by creditworthy firms.

questions.q: Data collected by an investigator for the first time for a specific purpose are called:
questions.exp: Primary data are original, first-hand data collected by the investigator.

questions.q: A curve showing combinations of two goods that give the consumer the same level of satisfaction is called:
questions.exp: All points on an indifference curve give equal utility, so the consumer is indifferent among them.

questions.q: The class mark of the class interval 10–20 is:
questions.exp: Class mark = (lower limit + upper limit)/2 = (10 + 20)/2 = 15.

questions.q: The median of the observations 12, 5, 18, 9, 25 is:
questions.exp: Arranged in order: 5, 9, 12, 18, 25; the middle (3rd) value is 12. (13.8 is the mean.)

questions.q: The value of an index number for the base year is always:
questions.exp: Base year prices/quantities are the reference, so the base year index is taken as 100.

questions.q: When marginal product (MP) is positive but falling, total product (TP):
questions.exp: TP rises as long as MP is positive; a falling MP means each extra unit adds less, so TP rises at a diminishing rate.

questions.q: If a consumer's income rises, the demand curve for an inferior good will:
questions.exp: For an inferior good, demand falls when income rises, so the demand curve shifts leftward.

questions.q: A consumer has an income of ₹100. Price of good 1 is ₹5 and price of good 2 is ₹10. With good 1 on the horizontal axis, the slope of the budget line is:
For the data X: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and Y: 10, 8, 6, 4, 2, the coefficient of correlation (r) between X and Y is:
questions.exp: Y falls by exactly 2 each time X rises by 1 (Y = 12 − 2X), a perfect negative linear relationship, so r = −1.

questions.topic: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.q: A perfectly competitive firm faces a market price of ₹8. Its minimum AVC is ₹10 and minimum AC is ₹12. In the short run, the firm should:
questions.a: Produce where price equals minimum AC
questions.b: Shut down and produce zero output
questions.exp: Price below minimum AVC means the firm cannot even cover variable costs, so it minimises loss by producing nothing.

questions.q: Mesopotamia developed between which two rivers?
questions.exp: 'Mesopotamia' means 'land between rivers', the Tigris and Euphrates in present-day Iraq.

questions.q: Who was the first Roman emperor, who established the 'Principate' in 27 BCE?
questions.exp: Augustus founded the regime called the Principate in 27 BCE, while keeping the fiction of a republic.

questions.q: The famous painting 'Mona Lisa' was made by:
questions.exp: Leonardo da Vinci, a Renaissance artist-scientist, painted the Mona Lisa.

questions.q: The People's Republic of China was established in 1949 under the leadership of:
questions.exp: The Chinese Communist Party led by Mao Zedong founded the People's Republic of China in 1949.

questions.q: The gold coin introduced by Emperor Constantine that remained in circulation long after him was the:
questions.exp: Constantine's monetary innovation was the solidus, a gold coin of 4.5 g that stayed in use for centuries.

questions.q: In medieval Europe, the land given by a lord to a knight in return for military service was called a:
questions.exp: A knight received a fief from his lord and in return fought for him; the tithe and taille were taxes.

questions.q: The swift courier system of the Mongol empire, which carried messages across vast distances, was called:
questions.exp: The yam was the Mongol postal relay system; the yasa was the legal code and the quriltai an assembly.

questions.q: The British declared Australia 'terra nullius' when they colonised it. This term meant:
questions.d: Land shared by settlers and natives
questions.exp: By calling it 'empty land', the settlers denied Aboriginal ownership and justified taking it.

questions.q: In 1517, Martin Luther launched a campaign in Germany that began the Protestant Reformation. His main target of criticism was:
questions.a: The printing of the Bible in the German language
questions.b: The spread of humanist education in universities
questions.c: The growing power of the Italian city-states
questions.exp: Luther argued that people did not need priests or purchased indulgences to reach God, challenging the Church's practice.

questions.q: The May Fourth Movement in China (1919) was a protest mainly against:
questions.a: The Meiji government's modernising reforms in Japan
questions.b: The Communist victory in the Chinese civil war
questions.c: Handing Germany's rights in Shandong to Japan
questions.d: The treaty ending the Opium Wars with Britain
questions.exp: Students protested in Beijing when the post-war peace conference handed Shandong, earlier held by Germany, to Japan.

Geography.book: Fundamentals of Physical Geography & India: Physical Environment

questions.q: The most abundant gas in the Earth's atmosphere is:
questions.exp: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the atmosphere by volume.

questions.q: The core of the Earth is made up mainly of:
questions.exp: The core is very dense and made of heavy materials, mostly nickel and iron (nife).

questions.q: U-shaped valleys are formed by the action of:
questions.exp: Glaciers erode the floor and sides of valleys, giving them a broad U shape; rivers form V-shaped valleys.

questions.q: The Standard Meridian of India passes through:
questions.exp: Indian Standard Time is based on 82°30'E longitude, passing near Mirzapur.

questions.topic: Solar Radiation, Heat Balance and Temperature
questions.q: The part of solar radiation that is reflected back to space without heating the Earth is called:
questions.exp: About 35 units out of 100 units of insolation are reflected back; this reflected amount is the albedo.

questions.q: Spring tides occur when:
questions.a: The Sun and Moon are at right angles to the Earth
questions.b: The Sun, Moon and Earth are in a straight line
questions.c: The Moon is farthest from the Earth
questions.exp: At new moon and full moon the three bodies are aligned, and their combined pull produces higher high tides.

questions.q: Pre-monsoon showers that help in the early ripening of mangoes, called 'mango showers', are common in:
questions.exp: Towards the end of summer, pre-monsoon showers in Kerala and coastal Karnataka are locally called mango showers.

questions.q: The Sundarbans in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta are named after the:
questions.exp: The Sundari tree, a mangrove species providing hard durable timber, grows abundantly there.

questions.topic: Solar Radiation, Heat Balance and Temperature
questions.q: The temperature at sea level is 30°C. Using the normal lapse rate of 6.5°C per km, the temperature at a height of 3 km would be about:
questions.exp: Fall in temperature = 6.5 × 3 = 19.5°C, so temperature = 30 − 19.5 = 10.5°C.

questions.q: In a limestone region, a geographer observes funnel-shaped depressions on the surface and caves with icicle-like deposits hanging from their roofs. The main agent forming these landforms is:
questions.exp: Groundwater dissolves limestone to form sinkholes and caves and deposits stalactites; this is karst topography.

Political Science.book: Political Theory & Indian Constitution at Work

questions.q: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution?
questions.exp: Dr B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee; Rajendra Prasad was President of the Constituent Assembly.

questions.q: In India's parliamentary system, the real executive power is exercised by the:
questions.a: President acting on his own judgement
questions.b: Vice-President as head of Rajya Sabha
questions.d: Council of Ministers led by the PM
questions.exp: The President is the nominal head; the Council of Ministers led by the PM actually runs the government.

questions.q: Members of the Rajya Sabha from the states are elected by the:
questions.b: Members of the Lok Sabha from that state
questions.c: Governors of the states on the CM's advice
questions.exp: Rajya Sabha members are indirectly elected by elected MLAs of each state.

questions.q: The Election Commission of India is provided for under Article:
questions.exp: Article 324 provides for an independent Election Commission to supervise elections.

questions.q: Reserving seats in jobs and education for historically disadvantaged groups is an example of:
questions.exp: Special measures to correct past disadvantage and promote equality of opportunity are called affirmative action.

questions.q: Which Fundamental Right prohibits the employment of children below 14 years in factories and mines?
questions.exp: Article 24, under the Right against Exploitation, prohibits child labour in hazardous work.

questions.q: The idea of deciding just principles from behind a 'veil of ignorance' was given by:
questions.exp: Rawls argued that people unaware of their future position would choose fair rules for all.

questions.q: The Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) is important because the Supreme Court:
questions.b: Banned all amendments to the Constitution
questions.c: Abolished the right to property as a Fundamental Right
questions.d: Ordered Parliament to create the Election Commission
questions.exp: The Court held that amendments cannot violate the basic structure of the Constitution.

questions.q: The Governor of a state reports that the government of the state cannot be carried on as per the Constitution. On this basis, President's Rule is imposed. This is done under Article:
questions.exp: Article 356 allows President's Rule when constitutional machinery fails in a state; 352 is national emergency and 360 financial emergency.

questions.q: A citizen challenges a new law in the Supreme Court, arguing that it violates Fundamental Rights. The Court declares the law unconstitutional and invalid. This power of the Court is called:
questions.exp: Judicial review is the power to examine laws and declare them void if they conflict with the Constitution.

questions.q: The term 'sociology' was coined by:
questions.exp: The French thinker Auguste Comte coined the term and is considered a founder of sociology.

questions.topic: Terms, Concepts and their Use in Sociology
questions.q: A group whose standards a person uses to evaluate himself, though he may not belong to it, is a:
questions.exp: People compare themselves with a reference group and try to imitate its lifestyle.

questions.q: Marriage in which a person has only one spouse at a time is called:
questions.exp: Monogamy restricts an individual to one spouse at a given time.

questions.q: Which of the following is a part of material culture?
questions.exp: Material culture consists of tangible objects and tools made by people; beliefs, values and customs are non-material.

questions.q: The invention of the steam engine, which transformed industry and transport, is an example of which source of social change?
questions.exp: New technology like the steam engine changed production and social life, an example of technological change.

questions.topic: Terms, Concepts and their Use in Sociology
questions.q: A working mother has an important office meeting at the same time as her child's school function. She is facing:
questions.exp: Role conflict arises when the demands of two or more roles of the same person clash.

questions.q: According to Durkheim, modern societies based on specialisation and interdependence of individuals are held together by:
questions.exp: Organic solidarity arises from the division of labour, where people depend on each other's different roles.

questions.q: The book 'Social Background of Indian Nationalism', which used a Marxist approach, was written by:
questions.exp: A.R. Desai analysed Indian nationalism in terms of the economic and class forces of colonial India.

questions.q: A researcher wants to know the opinions of 2,000 people across five states on online shopping. She gives all of them the same set of written questions. The method used is:
questions.exp: A survey collects standardised information from a large sample using the same questionnaire.

questions.q: Rohan is fined by the traffic police for jumping a red light. Later, his friends make fun of him for it. Which statement is correct?
questions.a: The fine is informal control; the teasing is formal control
questions.b: Both are forms of formal control
questions.c: The fine is formal control; the teasing is informal control
questions.d: Both are forms of informal control
questions.exp: Formal control uses official agencies and laws (the police fine); informal control works through peers, ridicule and disapproval.

questions.q: Psychology is best defined as the science of:
questions.b: The soul and life after death only
questions.c: The structure of the nervous system only
questions.d: Social institutions such as family and state
questions.exp: Psychology systematically studies mental processes, experiences and behaviour in different contexts.

questions.q: In Maslow's hierarchy of needs, which needs form the base (lowest level) that must be met first?
questions.exp: Maslow placed basic physiological needs such as hunger and thirst at the bottom; self-actualisation is at the top.

questions.q: Which receptor cells of the retina are responsible for colour vision?
questions.exp: Cones work in bright light and allow colour vision; rods work in dim light.

questions.q: The 'forgetting curve', based on experiments with nonsense syllables, was given by:
questions.exp: Ebbinghaus found that forgetting is rapid at first and then slows down.

questions.q: At a noisy party, you focus on your friend's voice and ignore other conversations. This is an example of:
questions.exp: Selective attention means choosing a limited number of stimuli from many available ones.

questions.q: A student is asked to list as many unusual uses of a brick as possible. This task mainly tests:
questions.exp: Generating many varied, original answers to one problem is divergent thinking, linked to creativity.

questions.q: According to Erik Erikson, the main psychosocial challenge of adolescence is:
questions.exp: Adolescents try to form a clear sense of who they are; failure leads to role confusion.

questions.q: A study finds a correlation of +0.8 between hours of study and exam marks. This indicates:
questions.d: That study hours definitely cause high marks
questions.exp: A value near +1 shows that as one variable rises the other tends to rise; correlation alone does not prove causation.

questions.q: A rat in a box learns to press a lever because pressing it switches off a mild electric shock. Its lever pressing increases. This is an example of:
questions.exp: Behaviour is strengthened because it removes an unpleasant stimulus; this is negative reinforcement.

questions.q: Rohan learnt Spanish words last year. After studying French this year, he finds it hard to recall the Spanish words. This forgetting is due to:
questions.exp: In retroactive interference, new learning (French) interferes with the recall of older learning (Spanish).

questions.q: Which of the following is a volatile memory?
questions.exp: RAM loses its contents when power is switched off, so it is volatile.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a valid identifier in Python?
questions.exp: An identifier cannot begin with a digit.

questions.q: Standard ASCII uses how many bits to represent a character?
questions.exp: Standard ASCII is a 7-bit code representing 2^7 = 128 characters.

questions.q: Presenting someone else's work or ideas as your own without giving credit is called:
questions.exp: Plagiarism is copying another person's work and claiming it as one's own.
range(1, 10, 3) starts at 1 and steps by 3 while less than 10: 1, 4, 7.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
def f(a, b=2):
    return a * b
print(f(3), f(3, 4))
questions.exp: f(3) uses default b = 2, giving 6; f(3, 4) gives 12.

questions.q: What is the output of: print(not (5 > 3) or 4 < 2 and True)
questions.exp: not True is False; 4 < 2 and True is False (and is evaluated before or); False or False = False.

questions.q: The octal number (17)₈ is equal to which decimal number?

What is the output of the following code?
L = [5, 3, 8, 1]
L.sort(reverse=True)
print(L.pop(1), L)
questions.exp: After sorting, L = [8, 5, 3, 1]; pop(1) removes and returns 5, leaving [8, 3, 1].

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
s = 'banana'
print(s.count('a'), s.find('n'), s.replace('a', 'o', 1))
questions.exp: 'a' occurs 3 times; the first 'n' is at index 2; replace with count 1 changes only the first 'a', giving 'bonana'.

questions.q: Which of the following is an input device?
questions.exp: A scanner sends data (images of documents) into the computer; the others are output devices.

questions.q: In a relation (table), the number of rows (tuples) is called its:
questions.exp: Cardinality is the number of tuples; degree is the number of attributes (columns).

questions.q: Which SQL command displays the structure (columns and data types) of a table?
questions.exp: DESCRIBE (or DESC) table_name shows the field names, types and constraints of a table.

questions.q: The technology that overlays digital information such as images or text on a live view of the real world is:
questions.exp: AR adds digital content onto the real environment, whereas VR replaces it with a fully simulated one.

questions.q: What is the output of: print(2 ** 3 ** 2)
questions.exp: The ** operator is right-associative: 3 ** 2 = 9, then 2 ** 9 = 512.

questions.q: The query SELECT * FROM STUDENT WHERE Marks BETWEEN 60 AND 80; displays students whose marks are:
questions.exp: BETWEEN is inclusive of both the lower and the upper limits.

questions.q: Which condition selects names that END with the letter 'a'?
questions.exp: % matches any number of characters, so '%a' means anything followed by a final 'a'; wildcards work only with LIKE.
get() returns the default 0 because 'z' is absent; 0 + 7 = 7.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
L = [2, 4, 6, 8, 10]
print(L[1:4], L[-2])
questions.exp: L[1:4] takes indices 1 to 3 → [4, 6, 8]; L[-2] is the second-last element, 8.

questions.q: The HR manager wants to list employees from table EMP whose Commission has not been entered yet (stored as NULL). The correct query is:
questions.a: SELECT * FROM EMP WHERE Commission IS NULL;
questions.b: SELECT * FROM EMP WHERE Commission = NULL;
questions.c: SELECT * FROM EMP WHERE Commission == NULL;
questions.d: SELECT * FROM EMP WHERE Commission LIKE NULL;
questions.exp: NULL cannot be compared with = or LIKE; the IS NULL operator must be used.

questions.q: The poem 'The Voice of the Rain' was written by:
questions.exp: 'The Voice of the Rain' is by the American poet Walt Whitman.

questions.q: In Ted Hughes's poem 'The Laburnum Top', which bird visits the laburnum tree?
questions.exp: A goldfinch comes to its nest in the laburnum and brings the silent tree to life.

questions.topic: The Ailing Planet: the Green Movement's Role (Hornbill)
questions.q: Who wrote 'The Ailing Planet: the Green Movement's Role'?
questions.exp: The essay is by jurist and economist Nani Palkhivala.

questions.q: In the play 'Mother's Day', Mrs Pearson exchanges personalities with:
questions.exp: Her neighbour Mrs Fitzgerald uses a spell to swap personalities with her; Doris and Cyril are her children.

questions.q: In 'Birth', how does Andrew Manson revive the apparently stillborn baby?
questions.a: By giving it an injection of a strong stimulant
questions.b: By rushing it to the nearest hospital in the city
questions.c: By wrapping it in a warm blanket near the fire
questions.d: By dipping it in hot and cold water in turn, and rubbing it
questions.exp: Andrew dipped the child alternately in hot and cold water and rubbed and pressed its chest until it breathed.

questions.q: In 'The Adventure', Professor Gaitonde finds himself in an alternative world where history changed because of a different result of the:
questions.exp: In that world the Marathas had won the Battle of Panipat, so the British never came to rule India.

questions.q: In 'Silk Road', the main aim of the narrator's journey through Tibet was to:
questions.a: Trade silk with Chinese merchants on the old route
questions.b: Climb Mount Everest from its northern side
questions.c: Complete a kora around Mount Kailash
questions.d: Study Tibetan monasteries in and around Lhasa
questions.exp: Nick Middleton travelled to Mount Kailash to perform the kora, a sacred circumambulation of the mountain.

questions.q: In Shirley Toulson's 'A Photograph', the poet's mother in the photograph was about:
questions.exp: The poem says the mother 'would have been a sort of twelve or so' when the beach photograph was taken.

questions.q: In 'The Tale of Melon City', after the king was hanged, how did a melon become the new king?
questions.a: The citizens voted for it in a public election
questions.b: An idiot passing the City Gate chose it
questions.c: The dead king's will named it as his successor
questions.d: The ministers drew lots among the city's fruits
questions.exp: The ministers decided the next man at the City Gate would choose the ruler; the idiot said 'A melon', so it was crowned.

questions.topic: The Ailing Planet: the Green Movement's Role (Hornbill)
questions.q: In 'The Ailing Planet', the author refers to four principal biological systems of the Earth. Which of these is NOT one of them?
questions.exp: The four systems named are fisheries, forests, grasslands and croplands; rivers are not listed.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of electric dipole moment?
questions.exp: Dipole moment p = q x 2a, so its unit is coulomb x metre (C m).

questions.q: A charged particle moves through a uniform magnetic field. The magnetic force on it is maximum when its velocity is:
questions.exp: F = qvB sin(theta) is maximum when theta = 90 degrees, i.e. velocity perpendicular to the field.

questions.q: What is the power of a convex lens of focal length 50 cm?
questions.exp: P = 1/f (in metres) = 1/0.5 = +2 D.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the nuclear force?
questions.a: Long-range and acts only between protons
questions.exp: The nuclear force acts only over a few femtometres and is nearly the same for p-p, n-n and n-p pairs.

questions.q: A parallel-plate capacitor is charged and then disconnected from the battery. A dielectric slab of K = 4 is inserted to completely fill the gap. The potential difference between the plates:
questions.exp: Charge Q stays constant while C becomes 4C, so V = Q/C becomes one-fourth.

questions.q: In Young's double-slit experiment, light of wavelength 600 nm is used, the slit separation is 0.3 mm and the screen is 1.5 m away. What is the fringe width?
A circular coil of 100 turns and radius 10 cm carries a current of 5 A. What is the magnetic field at its centre? (mu0 = 4 pi x 10^-7 T m A^-1)
Lenz's law, which gives the direction of induced current, is a consequence of the law of conservation of:
questions.exp: The induced current opposes the change causing it, so work must be done to produce it; otherwise energy would be created from nothing.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: An electron starting from rest is accelerated through a potential difference of 100 V. What is its de Broglie wavelength approximately?
questions.exp: lambda = 1.227/sqrt(V) nm = 1.227/sqrt(100) = 0.1227 nm, i.e. about 0.123 nm.

questions.q: A 100 microfarad capacitor is connected to a 220 V, 50 Hz AC supply. What is the approximate rms current in the circuit?
Which of the following concentration terms does NOT change with temperature?
questions.exp: Molality is moles of solute per kg of solvent; mass does not change with temperature, unlike volume.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of conductivity (kappa)?
questions.exp: Conductivity is the reciprocal of resistivity (ohm m), so its unit is S m^-1.

questions.q: Lanthanoid contraction is mainly caused by:
