questions.a: increase in the number of electron shells
questions.exp: 4f electrons shield each other poorly, so the effective nuclear charge rises and atomic/ionic size steadily decreases.

questions.q: Deficiency of which vitamin causes scurvy?
questions.exp: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) deficiency causes scurvy, with bleeding gums.

questions.q: For a zero order reaction, the half-life is:
questions.d: proportional to the square of initial concentration
questions.exp: For zero order, t1/2 = [R]0 / 2k, so it is directly proportional to [R]0.

questions.q: How many unpaired electrons are present in the complex ion [Fe(CN)6]3-?
questions.exp: Fe3+ is d5; CN- is a strong-field ligand, so electrons pair up in t2g (t2g^5 eg^0), leaving 1 unpaired electron.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most acidic?
questions.exp: The electron-withdrawing -NO2 group stabilises the phenoxide ion, making 4-nitrophenol more acidic than phenol, p-cresol and ethanol.

questions.q: Hinsberg's reagent, used to distinguish primary, secondary and tertiary amines, is:
questions.exp: Benzenesulphonyl chloride reacts differently with 1 degree, 2 degree and 3 degree amines, which forms the basis of the Hinsberg test.

questions.q: 1.8 g of glucose (molar mass 180 g mol^-1) is dissolved in 100 g of water. Kb for water = 0.52 K kg mol^-1. What is the elevation in boiling point?
questions.exp: Molality = (1.8/180)/0.1 = 0.1 mol kg^-1; delta Tb = Kb x m = 0.52 x 0.1 = 0.052 K.

questions.q: A current of 2 A is passed through CuSO4 solution for 965 s. What mass of copper is deposited at the cathode? (Cu = 63.5 g mol^-1, F = 96500 C mol^-1)
questions.exp: Q = 2 x 965 = 1930 C = 0.02 F; Cu2+ needs 2 F per mole, so 0.01 mol x 63.5 = 0.635 g.

questions.q: In human females, fertilisation normally takes place in the:
questions.c: ampullary region of the fallopian tube
questions.exp: The ovum and sperm meet in the ampullary region of the fallopian tube (oviduct), where fertilisation occurs.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a stop codon?
questions.exp: AUG is the start codon (codes for methionine); UAA, UAG and UGA are stop codons.

questions.q: Darwin's finches of the Galapagos Islands are an example of:
questions.exp: From one ancestral seed-eating finch, many forms with different beaks evolved to use different habitats: adaptive radiation.

questions.q: An interaction in which one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited is called:
questions.exp: In commensalism (+, 0) one species gains and the other is unaffected, e.g. an orchid growing on a mango branch.

questions.q: The proteins encoded by the genes cryIAc and cryIIAb control which pests?
questions.exp: cryIAc and cryIIAb code for Bt toxins that control cotton bollworms; cryIAb controls corn borer.

questions.q: A man with blood group A (genotype IAi) marries a woman with blood group B (genotype IBi). What is the probability that their child has blood group O?
questions.exp: Each parent passes i with probability 1/2, so ii (group O) = 1/2 x 1/2 = 1/4.

questions.q: The large holes in Swiss cheese are due to carbon dioxide produced by the bacterium:
questions.exp: Propionibacterium sharmanii produces a large amount of CO2 during ripening, which forms the holes.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of ex situ conservation?
questions.exp: Seed banks preserve genetic material outside the natural habitat; the others protect species in their natural habitats (in situ).

questions.q: A double-stranded DNA sample contains 20% adenine. What percentage of its bases are guanine?
questions.exp: By Chargaff's rule A = T = 20%, so G + C = 60% and G = C = 30%.

questions.q: In a food chain, producers fix 10,000 J of energy. Following the 10 per cent law, how much energy is available to the tertiary consumers?
questions.exp: 10,000 J (producers) -> 1000 J (primary) -> 100 J (secondary) -> 10 J (tertiary consumers).

questions.q: On the set A = {1, 2, 3}, the relation R = {(1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 3)} is:
questions.exp: The identity relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, so it is an equivalence relation.

questions.q: If A is a 2 x 3 matrix and B is a 3 x 4 matrix, what is the order of AB?
questions.exp: (2 x 3)(3 x 4) gives a matrix of order 2 x 4, since the inner orders match.

questions.q: The function f(x) = e^x on the set of real numbers is:
questions.exp: f'(x) = e^x > 0 for all real x, so f is strictly increasing.

questions.q: What is the unit vector in the direction of the vector 3i + 4j?
questions.exp: Magnitude = sqrt(9 + 16) = 5, so the unit vector is (3i + 4j)/5.

questions.q: What is the value of the integral of cos^2 x dx from 0 to pi/2?
questions.exp: cos^2 x = (1 + cos 2x)/2; integrating from 0 to pi/2 gives (1/2)(pi/2) + 0 = pi/4.

questions.q: What is the area of the region enclosed between the curves y = x^2 and y = x?
questions.exp: The curves meet at x = 0 and x = 1; area = integral of (x - x^2) from 0 to 1 = 1/2 - 1/3 = 1/6.

questions.q: The general solution of the differential equation dy/dx = y is:
questions.exp: Separating variables: dy/y = dx gives log|y| = x + c, so y = Ce^x.

questions.q: For what value of k are the lines (x - 1)/2 = (y - 2)/3 = (z - 3)/k and x/1 = y/2 = z/2 perpendicular?
questions.exp: Perpendicular lines satisfy a1a2 + b1b2 + c1c2 = 0: 2(1) + 3(2) + k(2) = 0, so 8 + 2k = 0 and k = -4.

questions.q: An open box is made from a square sheet of side 18 cm by cutting equal squares from each corner and folding up the sides. What side of the cut square gives the box maximum volume?
questions.exp: V = x(18 - 2x)^2; V' = (18 - 2x)(18 - 6x) = 0 gives x = 3 (x = 9 is impossible), and V'' < 0 there, so x = 3 cm (V = 432 cm^3).

questions.q: A fair die is thrown three times. What is the probability of getting at least one six?
questions.exp: P(no six in 3 throws) = (5/6)^3 = 125/216, so P(at least one six) = 1 - 125/216 = 91/216.

questions.q: In the absence of a partnership deed, interest on a loan given by a partner to the firm is allowed at:
questions.exp: Under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, a partner's loan earns interest at 6% p.a. when there is no deed.

questions.q: On the retirement of a partner, the gaining ratio is calculated as:
questions.exp: Continuing partners gain the retiring partner's share, so gain = new share - old share.

questions.q: Debenture holders of a company are its:
questions.exp: A debenture is an acknowledgement of debt, so debenture holders are creditors who receive interest, not owners.

questions.q: Under Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013, goodwill is shown in the balance sheet under:
questions.exp: Goodwill is an intangible asset, shown under Non-current assets > Property, Plant and Equipment and Intangible Assets.

questions.q: A partner withdrew Rs 2,000 at the beginning of every month for a year. Interest on drawings is charged at 6% p.a. What is the interest on drawings?
questions.exp: Total drawings = Rs 24,000; average period for beginning-of-month drawings = 6.5 months; 24,000 x 6/100 x 6.5/12 = Rs 780.

questions.q: 100 shares of Rs 10 each (Rs 8 called up) were forfeited because the holder failed to pay the first call of Rs 3. How much is credited to Share Forfeiture Account?
questions.exp: Amount actually received = Rs 8 - Rs 3 = Rs 5 per share; 100 x 5 = Rs 500 is credited to Share Forfeiture A/c.

questions.q: For a non-financial company, dividend received on investments is classified in the Cash Flow Statement as:
questions.exp: For a non-financial company, dividends and interest received are returns on investments, so they are investing activities.

questions.q: Cost of revenue from operations is Rs 3,00,000, opening inventory Rs 50,000 and closing inventory Rs 70,000. What is the inventory turnover ratio?

questions.topic: Reconstitution of Partnership: Death of a Partner
questions.q: A partner with a 1/4 share died on 30 June. The firm closes accounts on 31 March, and his share of profit till death is based on last year's profit of Rs 60,000. What is his share of profit?
questions.exp: Period 1 April to 30 June = 3 months; 60,000 x 3/12 x 1/4 = Rs 3,750.

questions.q: A company issued 1,000 debentures of Rs 100 each at a 5% discount, redeemable at a 10% premium. What is the total loss on issue of debentures?
questions.exp: Discount = 1,000 x 5 = Rs 5,000 and premium on redemption = 1,000 x 10 = Rs 10,000; total loss = Rs 15,000.

questions.q: Coordination is described as:
questions.exp: Coordination is not a separate function; it runs through all functions at all levels, so it is called the essence of management.

questions.q: Span of management refers to:
questions.a: the number of levels in an organisation
questions.b: the number of subordinates a superior can effectively manage
questions.d: the period for which a manager is appointed
questions.exp: Span of management is the number of subordinates that can be effectively managed by one superior.

questions.q: Which of the following is an internal source of recruitment?
questions.exp: Transfer shifts an existing employee to another job, so it is an internal source; the others bring in outsiders.

questions.q: Which quality certification mark is used for agricultural products in India?
questions.exp: AGMARK certifies agricultural produce; ISI is for industrial products and Hallmark for gold jewellery.

questions.q: A plan that lays down the exact routine steps, in chronological order, for carrying out an activity is called a:
questions.exp: Procedures are routine steps specifying the exact manner and sequence in which work is to be performed.

questions.q: Trading on equity (financial leverage) is favourable to equity shareholders when:
questions.a: the rate of return on investment is higher than the rate of interest on debt
questions.b: the rate of interest on debt is higher than the return on investment
questions.exp: If ROI exceeds the cost of debt, the extra earnings from borrowed funds raise earnings per share.

questions.q: The 'grapevine' in an organisation is a form of:
questions.exp: Grapevine arises from social interaction outside official channels, so it is informal communication.

questions.q: A distribution channel of the form Manufacturer -> Retailer -> Consumer is called a:
questions.exp: There is one intermediary (the retailer) between manufacturer and consumer, so it is a one-level channel.

questions.q: In a factory, workers on the packing line receive orders from both the production supervisor and the quality supervisor. The orders often conflict, and workers do not know whom to obey. Which principle of Fayol is being violated?
questions.exp: Unity of command says each employee should receive orders from only one superior; dual subordination causes confusion.

questions.q: Sunrise Ltd needs more funds. It offers new shares only to its existing shareholders, in proportion to the shares they already hold, at a price below the market price. Which method of floatation is this?
questions.exp: A rights issue gives existing shareholders the privilege to buy new shares in proportion to their current holding.

questions.q: Which of the following is a flow variable?
questions.exp: National income is measured over a period of time (a year), so it is a flow; the others are measured at a point of time.

questions.q: Which function of money removes the problem of double coincidence of wants?
questions.exp: As a medium of exchange, money splits barter into separate sale and purchase, so wants need not coincide.

questions.topic: Indian Economy on the Eve of Independence
questions.q: At the time of independence, the largest share of India's workforce was engaged in:
questions.exp: About 70-75% of the workforce depended on agriculture at independence.

questions.q: India's New Economic Policy was announced in the year:
questions.exp: The New Economic Policy was introduced in 1991 in response to a balance of payments crisis.

questions.q: Primary deficit is equal to:
questions.exp: Primary deficit removes interest on past borrowing from fiscal deficit, showing current borrowing needs.

questions.q: Under a flexible exchange rate system, the rupee price of one US dollar rises from Rs 80 to Rs 85. The rupee has:
questions.exp: More rupees are needed per dollar, so the rupee has lost value; under market forces this is depreciation (devaluation applies to fixed rates).

questions.q: NABARD, the apex body coordinating rural financing institutions, was set up in:
questions.exp: NABARD was established in 1982 to coordinate all institutions involved in rural finance.

questions.q: The legal reserve ratio is 20% and fresh deposits of Rs 1,000 are made in banks. What is the maximum total deposit that can be created?
questions.exp: Money multiplier = 1/LRR = 1/0.2 = 5; total deposits = 1,000 x 5 = Rs 5,000.

questions.q: A firm's value of output is Rs 1,000 crore, intermediate consumption Rs 400 crore, depreciation Rs 50 crore and net indirect taxes Rs 30 crore. What is its net value added at factor cost?
In an economy, C = 100 + 0.75Y and investment I = 200 (Rs crore). What is the equilibrium level of income?
questions.exp: Y = C + I gives Y = 100 + 0.75Y + 200, so 0.25Y = 300 and Y = Rs 1,200 crore.

questions.topic: Bricks, Beads and Bones: The Harappan Civilisation
questions.q: The Great Bath was found at which Harappan site?
questions.exp: The Great Bath is a large tank in the Citadel of Mohenjodaro, probably used for ritual bathing.

questions.q: The project to prepare a critical edition of the Mahabharata, begun in 1919, was led by:
questions.exp: The noted Sanskritist V.S. Sukthankar led the team that prepared the critical edition of the Mahabharata.

questions.q: Where did the Buddha deliver his first sermon?
questions.exp: The Buddha gave his first sermon at Sarnath near Varanasi.

questions.q: The ruins at Hampi were brought to light in 1800 by an engineer and antiquarian named:
questions.exp: Colin Mackenzie, an employee of the English East India Company, prepared the first survey map of Hampi.

questions.q: Ibn Battuta described two plants unfamiliar to his readers that he saw in India. They were:
questions.exp: Ibn Battuta vividly described the coconut and the paan (betel leaf), which were new to his audience.

questions.q: The Alvars of Tamil Nadu were devotees of:
questions.exp: The Alvars were devotees of Vishnu, while the Nayanars were devotees of Shiva.

questions.q: Awadh was annexed by the British in 1856 on the ground that:
questions.a: the ruler had no natural heir
questions.b: it had refused a Subsidiary Alliance
questions.exp: Lord Dalhousie annexed Awadh in 1856 claiming the territory was being misgoverned.

questions.q: In Mughal agrarian society, the term 'khud-kashta' referred to:
questions.exp: Khud-kashta were residents of the village who held lands there; pahi-kashta were non-resident cultivators.

questions.q: A long Sanskrit inscription composed by the court poet Harishena praises a Gupta ruler as equal to the gods and lists his conquests. Which inscription is it?
questions.exp: The Prayaga Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar inscription) was composed by Harishena in praise of Samudragupta.

questions.topic: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
questions.q: In February 1922, a crowd of peasants set fire to a police station, killing several policemen. This led Gandhiji to call off the Non-Cooperation Movement. Where did this happen?
questions.exp: The violence at Chauri Chaura (in present-day Uttar Pradesh) made Gandhiji withdraw the movement.

Geography.book: Fundamentals of Human Geography & India: People and Economy

questions.q: The ratio between the number of people and the size of land is called:
questions.exp: Population density = number of people / area, usually per square km.

questions.q: In nomadic herding, 'transhumance' means:
questions.a: seasonal movement of herders and animals between plains and mountain pastures
questions.b: permanent settlement of herders in towns
questions.c: rearing animals in sheds using fodder
questions.exp: Transhumance is the seasonal migration of herders with their animals, e.g. to mountain pastures in summer and plains in winter.

questions.q: Footloose industries are industries that:
questions.a: depend on a single heavy raw material
questions.d: can be located in a wide variety of places
questions.exp: Footloose industries use small, light components and are not tied to a specific raw material, so they can locate almost anywhere.

questions.q: The World Trade Organisation (WTO) came into existence in:
questions.exp: The WTO was set up on 1 January 1995, replacing GATT (1948).

questions.q: The Trans-Siberian Railway connects:
questions.exp: The Trans-Siberian Railway runs from St Petersburg in the west to Vladivostok on the Pacific coast.

questions.q: In India's land-use categories, land left uncultivated for more than five years is classified as:
questions.exp: Culturable waste-land is land left uncultivated for over five years; it can be reclaimed.

questions.q: Which of the following is a ferrous mineral?
questions.exp: Manganese is used with iron in steel-making and is a ferrous mineral; copper and bauxite are non-ferrous, mica is non-metallic.

questions.q: The Human Development Index is based on which three key areas?
questions.a: Health, education and access to resources
questions.exp: HDI ranks countries on health (life expectancy), education (literacy and schooling) and access to resources (income).

questions.q: India's population was about 102.9 crore in 2001 and 121.1 crore in 2011. What was the approximate decadal growth rate?

Ms Rao is the chief executive of a multinational company. She spends her day making high-level policy decisions and interpreting new ideas and data that affect the firm worldwide. Her work belongs to which type of activity?
questions.exp: Quinary activities are top-level decision-making and policy roles of senior executives and officials ('gold collar' professions).

Political Science.book: Contemporary World Politics & Politics in India since Independence

questions.q: What is the common currency used by many members of the European Union?
questions.exp: The euro is the common currency adopted by many EU member states.

questions.topic: The United Nations and its Organisations
questions.q: How many permanent members does the UN Security Council have?
questions.exp: The five permanent members are the USA, UK, France, Russia and China, each with veto power.

questions.q: Bangladesh emerged as an independent country in:
questions.exp: East Pakistan became independent Bangladesh in December 1971.

questions.q: The first meeting of the World Social Forum was held in 2001 at:
questions.exp: The WSF, an open platform opposing neo-liberal globalisation, first met in Porto Alegre, Brazil, in 2001.

questions.q: The principle of 'common but differentiated responsibilities' in environmental agreements means that:
questions.a: all countries must cut emissions equally
questions.c: developed countries bear greater responsibility given their historical emissions
questions.d: responsibility lies only with the UN
questions.exp: All share responsibility, but developed countries, having contributed more to the problem, must do more.

questions.q: The national emergency declared on 25 June 1975 on grounds of 'internal disturbance' was under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.exp: Article 352 provides for a national emergency; the 1975 emergency cited internal disturbance.

questions.q: The Anandpur Sahib Resolution of 1973 is associated with regional aspirations in:
questions.exp: Passed by the Akali Dal, it asserted regional autonomy and Sikh interests in Punjab.

questions.topic: Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System
questions.q: Which slogan did Indira Gandhi use in the 1971 Lok Sabha elections?
questions.exp: Indira Gandhi's positive programme 'Garibi Hatao' helped Congress (R) win a big victory in 1971.

questions.q: In 1990, the Central Government decided to implement the Mandal Commission recommendation of 27% reservation for OBCs in central government jobs. Which Prime Minister's government took this decision?
questions.exp: The National Front government led by V.P. Singh decided in August 1990 to implement the Mandal recommendations.

questions.q: In 1972, the USA and the USSR signed the Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty, which limited but did not ban their use of missile defence systems. This is an example of:
questions.exp: Arms control regulates the acquisition or development of weapons; disarmament requires giving them up altogether.

Sociology.book: Indian Society & Social Change and Development in India

questions.topic: The Demographic Structure of the Indian Society
questions.q: Birth rate is the number of live births in a given area during a year per how many population?
questions.exp: Birth rate is expressed as live births per 1,000 population per year.

questions.q: A family in which property and the family name pass from father to son is called:
questions.exp: In patrilineal families descent and inheritance are traced through the male line.

questions.topic: The Market as a Social Institution
questions.q: The idea of the 'invisible hand' of the market is associated with:
questions.exp: Adam Smith argued that individuals pursuing self-interest are guided by an 'invisible hand' to benefit society.

questions.q: An identity based on the accident of birth, such as caste or community, rather than on choice or achievement is called:
questions.exp: Community identities are ascriptive because they are acquired by birth, not by choice or accomplishment.

questions.q: Under colonial rule, some old trading towns declined while new colonial port cities grew. Which of the following older towns declined?
questions.exp: Older trading cities like Surat and Masulipatnam declined, while colonial cities like Bombay, Madras and Calcutta grew.

questions.topic: Change and Development in Rural Society
questions.q: The Green Revolution was first introduced mainly in areas that:
questions.exp: HYV seeds needed assured water, so it was introduced in irrigated regions such as Punjab, western UP and coastal Andhra Pradesh.

questions.topic: Change and Development in Industrial Society
questions.q: Which thinker argued that workers under capitalism experience alienation, as they have no control over their work or its products?
questions.exp: Karl Marx held that industrial capitalism alienates workers from their work, its product and themselves.

questions.q: When a foreign TV channel starts broadcasting in Hindi and adapts its shows to Indian festivals, this mixing of global and local culture is called:
questions.exp: Glocalisation is the blending of the global with the local, often as a strategy of global firms to suit local cultures.

questions.topic: The Demographic Structure of the Indian Society
questions.q: In a region, there are 300 people aged below 15 years, 600 aged 15-64 years and 60 aged above 64 years. What is the dependency ratio (per 100 working-age persons)?
questions.exp: Dependency ratio = (dependants / working-age population) x 100 = (300 + 60)/600 x 100 = 60.

questions.q: A state government funds the upkeep of historic temples, mosques and churches alike and does not favour any one faith. This reflects the Indian meaning of secularism, which is:
questions.b: a complete ban on religion in public life
questions.c: state support to the majority religion
questions.d: equal respect by the state for all religions
questions.exp: In India, secularism mainly means the state treats all religions equally, unlike the Western idea of strict separation.

questions.q: The theory of multiple intelligences was proposed by:
questions.exp: Howard Gardner proposed that there are several independent types of intelligence, such as linguistic and spatial.

questions.q: People who are highly motivated, impatient and always feel short of time are described as having:
questions.exp: Friedman and Rosenman described Type A people as ambitious, impatient and time-pressured.

questions.q: An irrational and persistent fear of a specific object, activity or situation is called a:
questions.exp: A phobia is an irrational fear of a specific object, place or situation.

questions.q: Behaving in a particular way in response to a request from another person, without any authority involved, is called:
questions.exp: Compliance is responding to a request; obedience is responding to a command from an authority.

questions.q: In client-centred therapy developed by Carl Rogers, the therapist mainly provides:
questions.exp: Rogers's therapy relies on empathy, warmth and unconditional positive regard to support the client's growth.

questions.q: The three components of an attitude (the A-B-C components) are:
questions.exp: Attitudes have an affective (feeling), behavioural (action tendency) and cognitive (thought) component.

questions.q: According to Kobasa, psychological hardiness consists of:
questions.exp: Kobasa described hardiness as the 3 Cs: commitment, control and challenge, which help people resist stress.

questions.q: Which projective test asks a person to describe what they see in a set of ambiguous inkblots?
questions.exp: The Rorschach test uses 10 inkblots; TAT uses picture cards, and MMPI and 16PF are self-report inventories.

questions.q: Rohan keeps getting thoughts that his hands are contaminated. He washes them dozens of times a day, knows it is excessive, but feels unable to stop, and it disturbs his studies. Which disorder is most likely?
questions.exp: Persistent unwanted thoughts (obsessions) with repeated uncontrollable acts (compulsions) indicate obsessive-compulsive disorder.

questions.q: A close-knit school committee wants quick agreement on a costly trip. Members with doubts keep quiet, no alternatives are considered and everyone assumes all agree. The plan fails badly. This is an example of:
questions.exp: Groupthink occurs when a cohesive group's desire for consensus overrides realistic appraisal of alternatives.

questions.q: Which built-in exception is raised when a number is divided by zero in Python?
questions.exp: Dividing by zero, e.g. 5/0, raises ZeroDivisionError.

questions.q: In which network topology are all nodes connected to a central switch or hub?
questions.exp: In a star topology each node connects directly to a central device such as a switch or hub.

questions.q: A candidate key that is not chosen as the primary key is called a(n):
questions.exp: Among candidate keys, one becomes the primary key and the remaining ones are alternate keys.

questions.q: Which Python module is used to write Python objects to a binary file and read them back?
questions.exp: The pickle module's dump() and load() serialise and deserialise Python objects for binary files.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
def f(a, b=2):
    return a ** b
print(f(3), f(2, 3))
questions.exp: f(3) uses the default b = 2, giving 3**2 = 9; f(2, 3) gives 2**3 = 8, so it prints 9 8.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
s = []
for x in [10, 20, 30]:
    s.append(x)
s.pop()
s.append(40)
print(s.pop(), s)
questions.exp: After pushing 10, 20, 30 the pop removes 30; pushing 40 gives [10, 20, 40]; the next pop returns 40, leaving [10, 20].

questions.q: A relation STUDENT has 5 attributes (columns) and 8 tuples (rows). What are its degree and cardinality?
questions.exp: Degree is the number of attributes (5) and cardinality is the number of tuples (8).

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
f = open("t.txt", "w")
f.writelines(["ab", "cd", "ef"])
f.close()
f = open("t.txt")
print(f.read(3), len(f.read()))
f.close()
questions.exp: writelines() adds no newlines, so the file holds 'abcdef'; read(3) gives 'abc' and the next read() returns the remaining 'def' of length 3.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
x = 5
def change():
    global x
    x = x * 2
    return x
print(change() + x)
questions.exp: change() is evaluated first: it sets global x to 10 and returns 10; then x is read as 10, so 10 + 10 = 20.

questions.q: Table STAFF has 6 rows. The column BONUS contains NULL in 2 of these rows. What does the query SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(BONUS) FROM STAFF; return?
questions.exp: COUNT(*) counts all 6 rows, while COUNT(BONUS) ignores NULLs and counts only 4.

questions.q: If no index is given while creating a Pandas Series, the default index labels start from:
questions.exp: Pandas assigns default integer index labels 0, 1, 2, ... when no index is specified.

questions.q: Which SQL function returns the number of characters in a string?
questions.exp: LENGTH('India') returns 5; COUNT() is an aggregate function that counts rows.

questions.q: Which network device sends data only to the intended destination port, using MAC addresses?
questions.exp: A switch forwards each frame only to the port of the destination device, unlike a hub that broadcasts to all ports.

questions.q: Presenting someone else's work or ideas as your own without giving credit is called:
questions.exp: Plagiarism is using another person's work without acknowledgement, a violation of intellectual property.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
import pandas as pd
s = pd.Series([10, 20, 30, 40], index=['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'])
print(s['b':'c'].sum())
questions.exp: Slicing with labels includes both ends, so s['b':'c'] has 20 and 30; their sum is 50.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({'A': [1, 2, 3], 'B': [4, 5, 6]})
df['C'] = df['A'] + df['B']
print(df.shape)
questions.exp: The DataFrame has 3 rows; adding column C makes 3 columns, so shape is (3, 3).

questions.q: What is the output of the query SELECT MOD(17, 5), POWER(2, 3); ?
